image.subject: the heavy chestnut front door of an old timber house in plain daylight, an iron bear knocker on the wood, the lock freshly cleaned

storyboard.claim: Preserving the old house threatens a family built on lies.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The chestnut front door and iron knocker of Peton in daylight, the house as the thing being protected.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Opens the final section on the museum threat to the Eldridge house.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the house itself as the object of preservation.

image.subject: an overgrown backyard marked off with string lines and small wooden stakes in a grid of squares, flat grey daylight, nobody in frame

storyboard.claim: A museum wants to dig up and catalogue the yard.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A gridded excavation survey laid over the overgrown backyard.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Turns the abstract preservation threat into the physical yard.
storyboard.addedInformation: The string grid shows the excavation plan.

storyboard.claim: The family legacy of murder and identity theft cannot survive historical accuracy.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Text card only: the claim stands without a picture.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Explains why the grid of digging is a threat to the family.
storyboard.addedInformation: Names the family's legacy as murder and identity theft.

image.subject: a man in his forties, neat build, short hair, tweed jacket, polite but intense, standing in a panelled hallway of an old house and holding a folded cheque

storyboard.claim: Henry's wealthy backers pay far above market value to preserve the house.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Henry in a tweed jacket holding a folded cheque in the panelled hall.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Introduces Henry as the face of the buying scheme.
storyboard.addedInformation: The cheque shows the money behind the museum deal.

image.subject: a curling instant snapshot of a large gilded oil portrait in a dim parlor, a stern heavy man in a dark wool coat with a white collar beside a young woman in a plain cap

storyboard.claim: The target item is a grand oil painting of Archie and Molly Eldridge in the parlor.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A snapshot of the gilded portrait of the stern man and the young servant woman.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Narrows the buying scheme to one object inside the house.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows what the painting depicts: Archie and Molly.

storyboard.claim: The museum wants to honor the founding family of Wood Haven, which is the sickest irony in the novel.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Text card only: the irony carried by the words.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Follows the painting and names the irony of honoring it.
storyboard.addedInformation: Frames the honor as an irony for the reader.

storyboard.claim: The benefactors will spend millions to save the painting.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Text card only: the large number is the picture.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Continues the painting sentence with the price.
storyboard.addedInformation: Puts a dollar scale on the painting deal.

image.subject: a gilded oil painting hung in a museum-lit room, a stern heavy man in a dark wool coat with a white collar, spotlight on the frame, no visitors

storyboard.claim: The benefactors are paying to preserve a portrait of a killer and an executed witch.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The gilded portrait lit like a museum piece under a spotlight.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Returns to the painting to name who it depicts.
storyboard.addedInformation: Museum lighting shows the portrait is being presented as a treasure.

image.subject: a young woman in her twenties, slim, long pale hair under a plain linen cap, dark period dress, frightened eyes, standing in a candlelit parlor and holding a dark lace mask at her side

storyboard.claim: The executed witch is dressed up as respectable upper class.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Caroline in her dark dress with a lace mask held at her side in candlelight.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Puts the executed woman in the room the painting shows.
storyboard.addedInformation: The mask shows the respectable front hiding the witch.

storyboard.claim: Some read Henry as the white knight trying to save the house.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Text card only: the counter-argument is spoken, not drawn.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Opens a counter-argument against the earlier view of Henry.
storyboard.addedInformation: Names the sympathetic reading of Henry.

image.subject: a bare bed in a low bedroom with an unpaid bill lying on the blanket, no people

storyboard.claim: Julia is broke and Henry offers her a way out of poverty.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Julia on a bare bed, tired, with an unpaid bill on her knee.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Shows the pressure that makes Henry's offer tempting.
storyboard.addedInformation: The bill shows the financial reason she is vulnerable.

storyboard.claim: Henry offers Julia a salaried job managing the estate for the museum.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Text list of the three parts of the offer.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Spells out the offer from the previous beat.
storyboard.addedInformation: Names the exact terms: a salary and the estate management role.

storyboard.claim: Is Henry preserving history or only curating a profitable aesthetic?
storyboard.concreteVisual: Text card only: the question is the picture.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Turns Henry's good-guy reading into a question.
storyboard.addedInformation: States the central question about Henry's motive.

image.subject: a paint roller resting on a tray beside a freshly painted grey wall, the corner still showing a dark stain beneath the new paint, empty room, daylight

storyboard.claim: Henry is a house flipper who paints over a toxic problem and sells at a markup.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A grey paint roller on a tray beside a wall with a dark stain showing through.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Answers the question with the flipper image.
storyboard.addedInformation: The stain under the paint shows the hidden problem.

storyboard.claim: Henry is deeply problematic, and Julia brings him the proof.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Text card only: the verdict and the setup for the proof.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Shifts from the flipper image to Henry's actual conduct.
storyboard.addedInformation: Introduces the physical proof Julia brings him.

image.subject: a weathered grey bone with dry soil still clinging to it, resting on a folded white cloth on a worn wooden table under soft window light

storyboard.claim: Julia brings Henry a human bone she found in the yard.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A dirt-streaked bone on a white cloth on a wooden table.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Gives the physical proof named in the previous beat.
storyboard.addedInformation: The cloth and table keep the find calm, not gory.

image.subject: a man in his forties in a tweed jacket leaning across a polished desk toward a woman in her thirties with shoulder-length dark hair, plain modern clothes, tired expression, his hand flat on the desk

storyboard.claim: Henry tells Julia to bury the bone again and refuses to exhume the corpses.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Henry leaning across a desk at Julia, his hand flat on the wood.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Shows Henry's response to the bone.
storyboard.addedInformation: The posture shows his pressure to cover it up.

left.label: INVESTIGATION
left.subject: yellow crime-scene tape stretched across a doorway of an old timber house

right.label: DEAL
right.subject: a for-sale sign planted in a lawn in front of a grey timber house

storyboard.claim: Henry chooses the real estate deal over an investigation of the bone.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Crime-scene tape on one side and a for-sale sign on the other.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Explains why Henry hides the bone.
storyboard.addedInformation: Sets the two outcomes side by side.

storyboard.claim: Henry cares only about a sanitized, profitable, curated history.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Text checklist of three words describing his history.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Describes the kind of history Henry cares about.
storyboard.addedInformation: Lists the three traits of his version of history.

image.subject: a glass museum display case under bright spotlight holding a neat row of antique silver candlesticks, a brass label plate beneath, no people

storyboard.claim: Henry would cover up a murder to build his museum exhibit.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A polished museum case of silver candlesticks under spotlight.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Connects Henry's cover-up to the exhibit he wants.
storyboard.addedInformation: The clean case shows the sanitized exhibit.

image.subject: a signed property deed on a desk with a fountain pen resting on it beside a brass key, under warm lamplight

storyboard.claim: The house corrupts Henry before the deed is dry, making him an accessory.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A signed deed, a fountain pen and a brass key under lamplight.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Moves from the exhibit to the signed purchase.
storyboard.addedInformation: The signed deed marks the moment he is bound to the house.

image.subject: an old household ledger open on a table, faded ink columns of figures, a candle burning beside it, the pages yellowed

storyboard.claim: The house keeps receipts and demands a cover up from everyone who touches it.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A yellowed household ledger of faded columns beside a candle.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Explains how the house keeps its record of the deed.
storyboard.addedInformation: The ledger is the house's own record of what it has kept.

image.subject: a deep rectangular trench cut into an overgrown backyard, dark wet soil heaped on the grass, a wooden shovel leaning on the pile, grey light

storyboard.claim: The earth releases the truth, and the timelines crash together in the final excavation.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A deep trench in the backyard with soil heaped beside it and a shovel leaning on the pile.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Turns the earth metaphor into the actual dig.
storyboard.addedInformation: The trench is the climax's physical location.

image.subject: a woman in her seventies, composed, grey-streaked hair, cardigan, cold expression, standing in a dim hallway of an old house with her hands folded

storyboard.claim: The police are called after Celia attacks Julia in the house and a man is found dead.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Celia standing composed in a dim hallway, cold expression, hands folded.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Shifts the story from the earth to the people inside the house.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows Celia as the composed figure at the centre of the attack.

image.subject: the imposing facade of an old timber house at night, red and blue emergency light washing over the chestnut front door and grey walls, no people

storyboard.claim: Red and blue police lights flash over Peton's imposing facade as the whole thing falls apart.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The house facade at night in red and blue flashing light.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Shows the police arrival in the house's own setting.
storyboard.addedInformation: The alternating light marks the collapse of the cover up.

image.subject: a row of portable floodlights on tripods lighting an overgrown backyard, two people in dark jackets digging with shovels into the grass

storyboard.claim: Police set up floodlights and start digging the backyard.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Floodlights on tripods and two people digging in the lit backyard.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Follows the police arrival with the dig itself.
storyboard.addedInformation: The floodlights make the dig public and official.

storyboard.claim: They expect two skeletons: the murdered Ethel and Caroline.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Text list of the two expected skeletons.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: States the expectation before the dig finds the truth.
storyboard.addedInformation: Names who they think is buried in the yard.

image.subject: a shovel blade striking a pale bone in dark soil under a flood light, bright spray of loose dirt

storyboard.claim: The shovels hit bone three times, not the expected two.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A shovel blade striking a pale bone in dark soil under flood light.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Breaks the expectation set by the list.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the moment the count goes wrong.

image.subject: three small numbered yellow evidence markers standing in a row on the trampled grass beside an open pit, grey daylight

storyboard.claim: Three distinct skeletons are pulled from the dirt.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Three numbered yellow markers in a row beside an open pit.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Gives the count after the shovels hit three times.
storyboard.addedInformation: The numbered markers show three separate finds.

image.subject: a gilded oil portrait in an ornate frame hung on a bare wall beside a museum placard, the subjects turned toward the room

storyboard.claim: You can curate the past, build museums, paint portraits, and invent ghost stories.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A gilded portrait beside a museum placard on a bare wall.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Turns the explanation toward the reader and the act of curating.
storyboard.addedInformation: The placard and portrait show the curated past as an object.

image.subject: close view of dark soil being turned by a trowel, the earth crumbling in thin layers, grey light

storyboard.claim: Once you dig, the earth decides what comes up, and the earth does not lie.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A trowel turning dark soil in thin crumbling layers.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Continues from the curated past to the earth itself.
storyboard.addedInformation: The turned soil shows the layers of the past.

image.subject: a white lab table under bright lights with three labelled plastic evidence bags and a clipboard beside them, nobody in frame

storyboard.claim: The dirt holds the objective truth, and forensics confirms the three skeletons.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Three labelled evidence bags and a clipboard on a white lab table.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Moves from the dig to the lab results on the three skeletons.
storyboard.addedInformation: The labels show the forensic confirmation of the three finds.
